title: On Design Space Exploration of Cache System in Multi-Chiplet Systems
problem: Multi-chiplet systems have complex cache hierarchies spanning multiple dies with varying topologies; existing design space exploration methods (NN-Baton, IntLP) fail to optimize cache subsystem performance or explore the full design space efficiently.
motivation: Post-Moore's Law manufacturing requires chiplet-based heterogeneous integration, but optimizing cache hierarchies across multiple dies with inter-chiplet interconnects remains a bottleneck for system performance.
method: The method proposes a bilevel optimization algorithm—a technique that solves two related optimization problems alternately. It builds mathematical models of cache miss rates (cache lookups that fail) and network latency (data transfer time between chiplets) based on cache hierarchy design and how chiplets are connected. It then alternates between optimizing the cache subsystem and the inter-chiplet network, both aiming to minimize concurrent average memory access time (C-AMAT, the average time to fetch data across chiplets working together), within cost and power constraints.
key_novelty: This introduces bilevel optimization (a technique for solving two linked design problems) for jointly designing cache hierarchies and chiplet interconnects to minimize concurrent average memory access time (C-AMAT).
contributions: Mathematical formulation of C-AMAT as functions of cache hierarchy and inter/intra-chiplet interconnect parameters
Bilevel optimization algorithm decoupling cache and interconnect subproblems for scalability
Achieves 39.7% execution time reduction vs AMD Zen 4 and 39.2% vs Intel Sapphire Rapids, 25.91% vs IntLP baseline

metrics.speedup: 39.7% execution time reduction vs Zen 4, 39.2% vs Sapphire Rapids, 25.91% vs IntLP

limitations: Not discussed—focuses on optimization algorithm without empirical limitations analysis.
primary_theme: Cache hierarchy optimization for multi-chiplet systems
